conventions: side_rule shorthand in part_decisions: "sided" = the registry has only .driver/.passenger keys; the key shown is the stem (see the sided-keys rule below). "one" = one unsided key; the side goes in the side field, null when not said. "center" = side is center.
Order of lookup: this file, then the registry by key, then a new draft in the registry pattern. Never contradict a key in this file; if you think one is wrong, keep it and say so in a question.

Part decision values: key from the registry = "existing"; key drafted before this run (status drafted_before or drafted_now here) = "decided_before"; key you draft yourself = "no_place" plus one proposal; no part can be told = "unknown" with key null.

Sided registry keys (door.front, trim.fender.front, trim.quarter, trim.mirror, light.headlight, light.taillight, glass.side.front, interior.seat.front, interior.door.panel.front, exterior.side, wheel.*, undercarriage.suspension.*): when the side is said, use the full registry key and repeat the side in the side field. When it is not said, write the stem (as listed in part_decisions), decision "unknown", side null. Never pick a side.
Unsided keys: side is "center" when the registry or this file marks the key center, the said side when the statement gives one, else null.
left/LH = driver, right/RH = passenger. "image left", "image right", "near", "far", "foreground", "upper right" are positions in the picture: side null.
Plural of a sided part ("front fenders", "both doors") = one claim per side.
"nose" on this car is the front bumper: trim.bumper.front. The valance below it is exterior.valance.front. A front spoiler is trim.spoiler.front.

A gap, seam, fit or separation between two parts is one claim on the first-named part with exterior.body.alignment ("hood-to-nose seam" = exterior.hood; "nose-to-valance separation" = trim.bumper.front). No gap keys are drafted for this car.

An unnamed small piece (flange, bracket, fitting, fastener) in an undercarriage or engine_bay photo is keyed at the scene key (undercarriage, engine.bay). In body_exterior or body_interior scenes an unnamed "panel", "lid" or "edge" gets part null / unknown; other statements about the same photo do not name it for you unless they say the same part.

Whole-surface statements in a body_exterior scene with no view named ("no rust on exposed exterior surfaces") use exterior.body. Use exterior.front / exterior.rear / exterior.side only when the statement itself says front, rear or side of the car.
Rust wording always goes to image_visible_rust_severity when a severity is said or it is an affirmed "none"; rust condition keys are used only when no severity is said.
Condition keys are used across zones whatever their prefix: exterior.paint.loss and the rust property apply to engine-bay and undercarriage parts too.

"Marks" of unstated cause = exterior.surface.discoloration; "scuff" = exterior.flag.scratch; "loss", "chip", "exposed" = exterior.paint.loss. Glossy = exterior.paint.glossy; never infer a paint stage from gloss or colour.

Hedges: "appears", "no obvious", "no definite", "is visible", "is resolved in this view" still make a claim. "cannot be assessed", "not established", "does not establish", "unresolved", "unverified", "unmeasured", "unknown" make none: that part of the statement goes to not_a_claim (reason) or question (when it asks what something is or what caused it).

An affirmed negative is a claim only where a property has a none value: rust (existing), image_visible_breakage and image_visible_leak (drafted). Other negatives ("no structural failure") go to not_a_claim.
A statement that both affirms something and hedges gets the claim plus a not_a_claim reason for the hedged half; the entry may also carry a question.
A statement that explains what a feature is not (factory openings are not perforation) or how this view relates to other photos is not_a_claim.

Scene receipt_document photos can show a print of the car: key what the print shows as usual. The capture day is the day the print was photographed, not the day the state held; say so in a question if a later step needs the date.
"said" is copied verbatim from the statement, at most 80 characters.
Two parts in one sentence sharing one state = two claims with the same "said".

Receipt lines: the part is what the line item is or fits on (lens, bezel, housing, gasket of a tail lamp = light.taillight with side from LH/RH; (PR) or (SET) with no side = stem / side null). Gauges and their harnesses = interior.gauge.cluster. Machine-shop labour lines key to the part worked on (heads = engine.cylinder.head, the rest = engine.block). A receipt line states a purchase, not a visible state.
Never use *.assessed.baseline, a score, or the component_assembly_map states as a value; whole-photo assembly goes to image_visible_assembly_state on "vehicle" or "engine.assembly".
Drafted keys: lower case, dots, general to specific, no side in the key. Check this file before drafting; if you must draft, write the proposal with nearest existing key.
